subject: Post-call: FinTechCo deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging) - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@fintechco.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & follow-ups — deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging)

Hi Alice — thanks for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few follow-ups so we can size the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

Key items you mentioned today that affect deployment choice:
- SSO: FinTechCo requires SAML-based SSO + SCIM provisioning for group sync (IdP: Okta).
- Key management: customer-owned keys preferred; current primary is AWS KMS. They also mentioned an HSM-backed key requirement for signing in a few workloads.
- Logging & retention: audit logs and request trace retention of 5+ years; logs should include token-level anonymized identifiers, user IDs, and request/response hashes.
- Network: VPC peering or private VPC options to avoid public egress for inference traffic.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and architecture review needed for procurement.

High-level recommendation based on this: Dedicated or Private deployment are the likely fits. Hosted API can meet some requirements quickly, but for customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed key ownership + long-term audit retention, Dedicated (with VPC and KMS integration) or Private (for bring-your-own-HSM and tighter network control) are more appropriate.

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm the SSO IdP details (SAML metadata) and whether SCIM write access is permitted for provisioning?
2) Confirm whether AWS KMS is acceptable for envelope key storage and whether FinTechCo requires HSM-backed key material vs. an HSM-backed KMS (e.g., CloudHSM-backed KMS).
3) Provide the team contact for security (cc'd is fine) and procurement so we can share SOC 2 and draft terms.
4) I'll loop in Marcus (solutions) and Stephanie (sales lead) to propose a technical kickoff once we get the SAML metadata and KMS clarification.

Attached: preliminary Dedicated pricing deck and our SOC 2 summary.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up call this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (PDF), SOC2_summary.pdf (PDF)

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@fintechco.com, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & follow-ups — deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and the clear next steps. Confirming a few points from our side:

- SSO/SCIM: We use Okta as our IdP. I'll attach the SAML metadata for the dev environment in a follow-up (security team will send the final production metadata once CNX is approved). SCIM provisioning is allowed but we prefer read/write be scoped to a service account.
- KMS/HSM: Our security team requires HSM-backed key material for signing. We currently use AWS KMS backed by CloudHSM for a subset of keys. For inference data we prefer envelope encryption with customer KMS keys; ultimate ownership must remain with FinTechCo.
- Logging: 5 years retention is our baseline for audit logs. We need the logs exported (immutable) to an S3 bucket under our account and also delivered to our SIEM. Logs must include request timestamps, anonymized request IDs, call latency, model version, and a redacted prompt hash.
- Network: VPC peering or Private VPC is required for production. For PoC we can use Dedicated with restricted egress if needed.
- Timeline: procurement wants final architecture and SOC 2 evidence by next Wednesday (2025-07-02) to hit the Q3 deployment window.

I'll have security send the SAML metadata and our KMS contact (kevin@fintechco.com). Procurement is looped here (procurement@fintechco.com) for contract/RFP steps.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Wong
Head of Platform Engineering | FinTechCo
alice.wong@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@fintechco.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, procurement@fintechco.com, security@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & follow-ups — deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging)

Thanks Alice — that's very helpful. I've looped Marcus (solutions engineering) and Stephanie (sales lead) to kick off the technical deep-dive. Quick answers and proposed plan below:

- SSO/SCIM: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0. We'll accept Okta metadata for both test and production. SCIM service account with scoped write access is the standard pattern we use.
- KMS/HSM: We support two common patterns:
  * Dedicated: customer-managed AWS KMS keys can be used for envelope encryption; Redwood manages the inference runtime keys but the envelope key is customer-owned. This works with CloudHSM-backed KMS.
  * Private (VPC/on-prem): for customers that require direct HSM integration (customer-hosted HSM or direct HSM appliance), Private gives the strongest control.
- Logging & retention: we can export immutable audit logs to your S3 bucket and integrate with common SIEMs (Splunk, SumoLogic) via delivery pipelines. Retention policies can be handled on your S3 lifecycle or by exporting to Glacier/Archive tiers for long-term retention.
- Network: VPC peering or Private VPC are both supported. For Dedicated we typically use a VPC peering + strict security groups and private endpoints. Private gives you a customer-run control plane and full isolation if required.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Marcus to run a short technical kickoff (30–45m) to review SAML metadata, KMS architecture (CloudHSM details), and logging/export mechanics. Please share Kevin's contact and the SAML metadata when ready.
2) We'll send a more detailed KMS integration note and an architecture sketch (attached) that maps Dedicated vs Private trade-offs for your security team.
3) We'll provide the SOC 2 Type II report and references via a secured link for procurement to review by 2025-07-01.

Marcus — can you take the lead on preparing the KMS integration note and be available for a tech kickoff tomorrow or Friday?

Thanks — attaching a short architecture sketch and the Dedicated pricing PDF again.

Best,
Marissa
Attachments: redwood-kms-integration-sketch.png (PNG), redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (PDF), SOC2_summary.pdf (PDF)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@fintechco.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, security@fintechco.com, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: KMS/HSM and logging notes — quick technical summary

Hi Alice / team — quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff:

1) KMS integration patterns we support:
   - Envelope encryption: Redwood runtime encrypts model state and KV cache with a local data key; that data key is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS CMK (AWS KMS). Customer keeps CMK ownership and rotation control.
   - HSM-backed KMS: If CloudHSM-backed KMS is used, we treat it the same as an AWS KMS CMK (no special code changes). If customers require direct HSM appliance access for signing/ attestations, Private deployment is recommended so the HSM can be network-attached to the inference hosts.

2) Logging/export:
   - We can stream audit logs to your S3 bucket (we write to a write-once prefix + manifest).
   - For immutability, customers can enable S3 Object Lock/Retention on the bucket.
   - We include the fields you requested: timestamp, anonymized request_id, latency_ms, model_version, prompt_hash (SHA-256), response_size. Payloads are redacted by default.

3) Network & firewall needs (production Dedicated):
   - VPC peering required with a couple of fixed IP ranges used for control-plane callbacks.
   - TLS mutual auth for service endpoints.
   - If Private, we coordinate on subnet sizing and host placement.

4) Next steps for the tech kickoff:
   - Please propose a 30–45m window tomorrow (Thu 2025-06-26) or Friday (2025-06-27). Kevin (KMS) + your security contact would be ideal.

If helpful, I can produce a one-page KMS checklist (required IAM roles, CMK policy snippets, S3 bucket policy + ObjectLock hints) before the call.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
Attachments: none
